name: Marina and the Old Town
tagline: Below the castle, where the yachts and the better restaurants are
description: The eastern end of the bay around the Netsel marina and the small Ottoman castle, with the old quarter's lanes climbing behind it. This is the more restrained side of Marmaris, with the sailing crowd, better restaurants and a working harbour rather than the club strip.
bestFor: Stays that want the marina and the old quarter, not Bar Street
pros: Best restaurants and the sailing community
The old town and castle immediately behind
Walkable to everything without being in the noise
cons: Busy with day visitors and gulet traffic

name: Marmaris Centre and Bar Street
tagline: The main strip, loud and cheap in season
description: The commercial centre behind the long beach, running back from the promenade to the bazaar, with Bar Street cutting through it. It is package-holiday territory and unapologetic about it, with the town's cheapest food, the bazaar and every service within a short walk.
bestFor: Short season stays that want the nightlife on the doorstep
pros: Everything, including the bazaar and the beach, within ten minutes
Cheapest eating and shopping in town
cons: Bar Street is genuinely loud until very late in season
Persistent touting on the main streets
Half of it closes from November

name: Icmeler
tagline: The quieter bay eight kilometres west, under the pines
description: A separate resort in its own bay ringed by pine-covered hills, with a cleaner beach and calmer water than Marmaris and a much more subdued evening. It has its own shops and restaurants, a long promenade, and dolmuses running into Marmaris every few minutes along the coast road.
bestFor: Stays that want the beach and the pines without the strip
pros: Cleaner beach and calmer water than the town
Pine-covered hills directly behind for walking
cons: Very quiet and largely closed out of season
Fifteen minutes to the town's services

name: Armutalan and Siteler
tagline: Where residents actually live, uphill behind the resort
description: The residential districts inland from the beach, with ordinary Turkish apartment blocks, local markets, schools and a year-round population that has nothing to do with tourism. Rents are a fraction of the seafront and the Tuesday market is here, which is the town's real shopping.
bestFor: Longer stays that want local prices and a neighbourhood that stays open in winter
pros: Rents well below anything near the water
The Tuesday market and everyday local shopping
Stays fully open through the winter
cons: Twenty minutes on foot down to the beach
No tourist services and little English

name: Selimiye and the Bozburun Peninsula
tagline: Fishing villages an hour south, for people who want out
description: The villages strung along the Bozburun peninsula south of Marmaris, of which Selimiye is the best known: a small bay with fishing boats, a handful of pensions and restaurants on the water, and almost nothing else. It is where people go when the resort becomes too much.
bestFor: Quiet stays on a working bay with a car and no need for a town
pros: Sailing and swimming straight off the shore
cons: An hour of winding road to Marmaris
Very limited services and slow internet
